A 61-year-old male patient visits his psychiatrist for a follow-up regarding treatment for schizophrenia.
He reports doing well but has recently noticed unusual movements in his face. His sister, who
accompanies him, mentions that he has become more withdrawn and continues to have conversations
when no one else is present. She also notes that despite changes to his medications during the past
three appointments, his symptoms have not improved. His vital signs include a temperature of 99.3°F
(37.4°C), blood pressure of 140/94 mmHg, pulse of 76/min, respirations of 16/min, and oxygen
saturation of 98% on room air. Physical examination reveals rhythmic movements of his mouth and
tongue. Which of the following is a potential side effect of the most appropriate next treatment? Answer
Choices: (A) QT prolongation on EKG (B) Akathisia (C) Hepatotoxicity (D) Orthostatic hypotension (E)
Infection (F) Worsening of psychotic symptoms (G) Dry mouth and dry eyes (H) Agranulocytosis (I)
Serotonin syndrome (J) Metabolic syndrome
 A. Serotonin syndrome
B. Dry mouth and dry eyes
C. Akathisia
D. Hepatotoxicity
E. Orthostatic hypotension
F. Agranulocytosis
G. Metabolic syndrome
H. Worsening of psychotic symptoms
I. QT prolongation on EKG
J. Infection
